main_text.p: Christiani, qui professionis Christianæ immemor, Edictum Imperatoris adversus fideles latum, & publico in loco Nicomediæ affixum arripuit, atque in minutissimas partes conscidit, cùm quidem ea in urbe uterque Imperator adesset: quo commisso facinore [illegible, ~3 letters] ἣν ὑ-τὸς πάθων[?] inquit Nicephorus, ut par erat pœnas pendit (reddente Johanne Lango) Licet enim illi certè digni,qui plura his paterentur, hic tamen indignus qui vel istud faceret. Quare, & utrumque Imperatorem satietate imperandi imperio se quidem abdicasse, neutrum autem à Marcellino Pontifice Romano abdicatum legimus, imò tantùm abfuit ab utrouis abdicando, ut unius suafu ipse Idolis thurificaret; quam Historiam, licèt & 1 Tom.1 conc. pag.222.{r}Binius &{f}Anno 302. num. 96Baronius, ut obreptitiam clarè refutari posse contendant: illam tamen veram fatetur Bellarminus, tum in Tractatu de Pontifice Romano, tum etiam in Epistola ad Blackwellum de Iuramento fidelitatis non susci-

page.notes: The Greek words on the first line are blurred and I could not read the first word; the second line ("τὸς πάθων") is also uncertain. The word split at the line end ("susci-") is partly unclear in the print. The reference marks "r" and "f" in the text match the margin notes. The margin note beside "Baronius" ("( Anno 302. num. 96") has a bracket before "Anno" that I took to be the mark "f". The left edge carries a fragment of the neighbouring page, which I left out.
